data: First US lunar orbiter (1966-08-14). Mapped potential Apollo landing sites; took the first photograph of Earth from lunar orbit — over two years before the famous Apollo 8 Earthrise

The first US spacecraft to orbit the Moon, four months after Luna 10. Launched 1966-08-10 from Cape Canaveral on an Atlas-Agena D, Lunar Orbiter 1 entered an elliptical lunar orbit on 1966-08-14. Its primary mission was to photograph candidate Apollo landing sites at sub-metre resolution — a 70 mm + 610 mm dual-lens camera system that developed film in-orbit (Bimat process) and scanned it for radio transmission to Earth. Captured the first photograph of Earth from lunar orbit (1966-08-23 — over two years before Apollo 8's more famous Earthrise) as a wide-angle shot taken during the 16th orbit. Returned 207 high-resolution + 207 medium-resolution frames mapping 4.1 million km² of the lunar surface. Deliberately crashed into the lunar far side on 1966-10-29 to clear the radio band for Lunar Orbiter 2.
First US lunar orbiter (1966-08-14); mapped Apollo landing sites and took the first photo of Earth from lunar orbit (1966).
Second US lunar orbiter (1966-11-10). Took the 'Picture of the Century' — oblique view of Copernicus crater at ~45 km altitude
Third US lunar orbiter (1967-02-08). Photographed Surveyor 1 sitting on the lunar surface — first photo of a spacecraft on another world
Fourth US lunar orbiter (1967-05-08). First polar lunar orbit; mapped 99 % of the near side at 60 m/pixel + far-side regions
Final US lunar orbiter (1967-08-05). Completed far-side mapping at 60 m/pixel; impacted 1968-01-31 ahead of Apollo lunar operations
First spacecraft to orbit another planet
